text.content: Architecture must be treated as a first-class classification dimension separate from System_Type, Functional Scope, Deployment and Licensing. Architecture describes how the system is structured and composed; integration is a related characteristic/capability that can be implemented through that architecture but should not be treated as a synonym for architecture. Current evidence supports recording architectural structure and integration relationships separately, while linking them where the evidence shows dependence.

text.content: A universal controlled vocabulary of Architecture types is not established. Do not normalize labels such as monolithic, modular, composable, microservices or three-tier as mutually exclusive system classes without product-specific and cross-source definitions. Integrations should be modeled separately from Architecture, with explicit distinction between internal/native integration and external/system-to-system integration. This separation remains a tested taxonomy design decision, not a completed Integrations taxonomy node.

text.content: Specific product classification remains context-sensitive and requires Vendor/Product/Edition/Plan/Version/Module/Localization/Market evidence when material. Version/localization and plan/edition can materially alter available accounting/reporting or operational scope without independently defining System_Type. Licensing is a separate descriptive/tiering and access/scope dimension; Singh (2006) documents its historical use in ERP tier classifications, but no direct universal licensing-to-System-Type rule is established. Mossa et al. (2025) notes multiple ERP interpretations, so this remains a working evidence-based classification framework rather than a universal ontology.
